name: Booking Holdings
description: Booking Holdings runs the world's largest online travel agencies: Booking.com (mainly hotel and apartment reservations), Priceline (North America), Agoda (Asia-Pacific), KAYAK (price comparison), Rentalcars.com and OpenTable (restaurant reservations). It earns a commission on bookings, mostly through the merchant model (the traveller pays Booking, which pays the hotel, 70 percent of revenue) and the agency model (the traveller pays the hotel; Booking bills a commission, 26 percent), plus advertising on KAYAK and other sites (4 percent). In FY2025 travellers booked $186.1B and Booking's revenue was $26.9B; adjusted EBITDA was $9.9B, a 37 percent margin. The company returns most of its cash: $3.7B of buybacks in Q2 2026 alone, on top of a dividend, after a 25-for-1 stock split in April 2026. It is in a $650M annual cost-savings programme through 2027 and faces AI-assistant competition and European regulation.

sub.name: Travel booking sites and ride apps

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge; not checked against an MSCI/S&P source. Booking owns no hotels: it is a fee-taking online travel agency.

hq.note: From general knowledge; not re-read from the 10-K cover. Booking.com itself is run from Amsterdam.

employees.note: FY2025 10-K: about 2,900 in the US and about 21,400 outside it

businessLines.name: Merchant revenue
businessLines.how: The traveller pays Booking at reservation; Booking pays the hotel later and keeps the difference plus payment-processing income. Merchant gross bookings were $130,025M (69.9%) of the $186,107M total in FY2025.

businessLines.name: Agency revenue
businessLines.how: The traveller pays the hotel directly; Booking earns a commission from the hotel after the stay. Agency gross bookings were $56,082M (30.1%) in FY2025.

businessLines.name: Advertising and other
businessLines.how: Advertisers pay for placement and referrals mainly on KAYAK, plus fees from other services (OpenTable, ancillary).

brands.name: Booking.com
brands.share: The 10-K says the majority of merchant revenue is Booking.com accommodation reservations; no percentage found

brands.name: Priceline
brands.share: Discount travel, North America; not broken out

brands.name: Rentalcars.com
brands.share: Rental cars: 23M rental car days in Q2 2026 (-6.5%)
